senses.definition: (heading, physical) To move or be moved into something.

subsenses.definition: (ergative) To descend or submerge (or to cause to do so) into a liquid or similar substance.
examples: A stone sinks in water.  The sun gradually sank in the west.

subsenses.definition: (transitive) To (directly or indirectly) cause a vessel to sink, generally by making it no longer watertight.
examples: An iceberg sank the Titanic.  British battleships sank the Bismarck.
The joint will hold tighter if you sink a wood screw through both boards.  The dog sank its teeth into the delivery man's leg.
